Know which computers, NAS, TVs or phones of your home network are on, and switch them on from
Gladys. Each watched host becomes a Gladys device that says whether it answers (online / offline)
and how fast (latency), with a **Wake up** button when its MAC address is known (Wake-on-LAN).

Typical uses: switch on the NAS before a backup and wait until it answers, see on the dashboard
that the kids' console is still on, know that a phone is home (presence), get warned when a
server stops answering.

> **Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome.** The integration is covered by automated
> tests, but has not yet been tried in a real Gladys installation with a real Wake-on-LAN
> computer. Tell us on the Gladys forum how it works with yours.

## What you get

- **One device per host**, with these features:

  | Feature     | Type in Gladys                | Shows                                                    |
  | ----------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Online**  | presence sensor (yes/no)      | green "presence detected" when it answers, red otherwise |
  | **Latency** | duration, in milliseconds     | average round trip of the last check (history chart)     |
  | **Wake up** | push button (only with a MAC) | **Push** sends the Wake-on-LAN packet                    |

- A **Network devices** dashboard widget: several hosts at a glance, with a **Wake** button for
  the ones that are off.
- A scene trigger, **A device did not wake up**, and two scene actions, **Wake a device
  (Wake-on-LAN)** (which can wait until the device answers) and **Check an address**.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant **5.1.0** or later.
- For the checks: hosts reachable from the Gladys machine, by **IP address** (a fixed one is best:
  reserve it in the DHCP settings of your router) or by a DNS name. `.local` names (mDNS) cannot
  be resolved inside the integration.
- For Wake-on-LAN:
  - the computer is on the **same local network** as Gladys, and preferably **wired** (Wake-on-LAN
    over Wi-Fi rarely works);
  - Wake-on-LAN is enabled in its **BIOS/UEFI** and in its system (Windows: properties of the
    network card, **Wake on Magic Packet**; turning off **Fast startup** often helps; Linux:
    `ethtool -s <interface> wol g`; NAS: power settings);
  - its **MAC address** (written on the router's list of devices, or `ipconfig /all`,
    `ip link`).
- At installation, Gladys asks you to allow two accesses: **Wake-on-LAN access** (the core sends
  the magic packets: the integration's container cannot send broadcasts) and **SSDP search for
  ssdp:all** (the network search).

## Configuration

### Settings

| Setting                           | Default   | What it does                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Check interval**                | 30 s      | How often every host is checked (15 s to 5 min).                                                    |
| **Offline after**                 | 1 minute  | Time without any answer before a host is shown offline. "At the first failed check" reacts at once. |
| **Wake-up timeout**               | 3 minutes | Time a woken device has to answer before **A device did not wake up** fires.                        |
| **Language of the feature names** | French    | Names of the features of new devices (Online, Latency, Wake up) and language of the messages.       |

### Adding a host

In **Integrations → Ping & Wake-on-LAN → Configuration**, fill in the **Add or update a host**
form and run it:

- **Name** and **IP address or host name** (required);
- **MAC address**, to get the **Wake up** button (any notation: `64:e4:d5:b4:12:66`,
  `64-E4-D5-B4-12-66`…);
- **Broadcast address**, only if the computer ignores the default wake-up (try the broadcast
  address of its network, e.g. `192.168.1.255`);
- **Check method**: **Automatic** (ping, then TCP when the ping gets no answer), **Ping (ICMP)
  only**, or **TCP port only**;
- **TCP port**: the port tried when the ping fails (e.g. 445 for a Windows PC, 62078 for an
  iPhone). Without it, the automatic method tries a few usual ports;
- **Offline after (this host)**: overrides the setting for this host (phones: 10 to 30 minutes).

The integration checks the host once and tells you whether it answers. Then open the **Discover**
tab and press **Add to Gladys**. To change a host, run the form again with the same name or the
same address: the device keeps its history. If the MAC address was added, press **Update** in the
**Discover** tab to get the button. **Remove a host** takes it out of the list (its device stays
in Gladys until you delete it).

### Network search

**Search the network** (and the **Scan** button of the **Discover** tab) asks Gladys for the
devices that announce themselves on the network (UPnP/SSDP: TVs, NAS, media servers, routers,
printers, game consoles, Windows PCs with network discovery on) and proposes them in the
**Discover** tab, named after their UPnP description. When the Gladys machine knows its MAC
address, the device comes with the **Wake up** button. Phones and most computers do not announce
themselves: add them by hand.

## Devices

- **Online**: 1 as soon as the host answers, 0 once it has not answered for the **Offline after**
  delay. A host never checked yet has no value.
- **Latency**: average round trip of the last check, in milliseconds, published again when it
  moves by 20 % (1 ms at least): the history stays readable. Nothing is published while the host
  is offline.
- **Wake up**: sends the Wake-on-LAN packet. The host is then checked every 5 seconds; a packet is
  sent again every 30 seconds while it stays silent, until it answers or the **Wake-up timeout**
  ends.

How a host is checked:

- **Ping (ICMP)**: three echo requests 0.2 s apart, 1 second to answer.
- **TCP**: a connection to a port. A refused connection proves the host is up too: only silence
  means offline. It catches the hosts that ignore pings (Windows firewall, some phones). Without a
  port, the automatic method tries 80, 443, 22, 445, 139, 3389, 5000, 8080, 8009 and 62078
  together.

Gladys shows "No recent value" on a value older than 48 hours: an unchanged state is published
again every 12 hours to avoid it.

## Dashboard widget

**Edit dashboard → add a widget → Network devices**. Leave **Devices shown** empty to see every
host (10 at most), or pick some. Each line gives the state of a host: **Online** with its latency,
**Offline**, or **Starting** after a wake-up. Up to four **Wake** buttons are shown for the
offline hosts that have a MAC address.

## Scene trigger

**A device did not wake up** fires when a device woken by the integration (button, widget or
scene) still does not answer at the end of the **Wake-up timeout**. The **Device** filter is
optional. Variables: **Device name**, **Address**, **Seconds waited**.

**Beware of loops**: a scene that wakes the device again on this trigger starts over at every failure, every few minutes, with no end (a computer unplugged from the mains will never answer). Send a message instead, or stop after one retry with a condition of your own.

For "the device is on / off", use the core trigger **Device state change** on the **Online**
feature, and tick **Execute only when threshold is passed**: the state is sent again every
12 hours, and without the box the scene would run again each time.

## Scene actions

- **Wake a device (Wake-on-LAN)**: **Device** (required) and **Wait until it answers**. Without
  waiting, the packet is sent and the scene goes on. With it, the next steps start once the device
  answers, or after 100 seconds (Gladys gives an action 120 seconds at most). Results:
  **Answering** (1 or 0) and **Start-up time** in seconds. A device already on is not woken
  (Answering 1, Start-up time 0).
- **Check an address**: an IP address or a host name (scene variables allowed) and an optional
  **TCP port** (then only this port is tried). Results: **Answers** (1 or 0) and **Latency**. No
  device is created.

The results are numbers (1/0) so that **Condition on variables** can compare them: choose the
result, **=**, and type `1`.

## Scene examples

1. **Backup on the NAS at night**: **Scheduled trigger** at 2:00 → **Wake a device** NAS with
   **Wait until it answers** → **Condition on variables**: Answering = 1 → your backup steps (for
   example **Make a HTTP request** to the NAS) → **Send Message** with the **Start-up time**
   result (insert it from the variable list).
2. **Movie evening**: in the scene that sets up the living room → **Wake a device** media PC
   (without waiting) → **Wait** 1 minute → turn on the TV.
3. **Server watch**: **Device state change** on **Online** of the server, value **No presence**, threshold
   box ticked → **Send Message** "The server no longer answers". A second scene on **A device did
   not wake up** → **Send Message** with the **Device name** and **Seconds waited** variables.

## Troubleshooting

- **A host stays offline although it is on**: it ignores pings (Windows firewall, phones). Use
  **Check method → TCP port only** with a port it opens (445 for Windows file sharing, 3389 for
  remote desktop, 22 for SSH, 62078 for an iPhone), or keep **Automatic** with that port.
- **A phone goes offline and back all the time**: phones asleep on Wi-Fi stop answering for
  minutes. Give the host **Offline after** 10 to 30 minutes.
- **The Configuration screen says that ping (ICMP) is not allowed**: the Docker of your Gladys
  machine does not let containers send pings (Docker older than 20.10). Hosts are then checked
  over TCP only: give each one a port, or update Docker.
- **Wake up does nothing**: check the MAC address, that Wake-on-LAN is enabled in the BIOS/UEFI
  and the system, and that the computer is wired. Try the broadcast address of its network. A
  computer that was unplugged from the mains often needs one normal start before Wake-on-LAN works
  again.
- **The network search finds nothing**: many devices do not answer SSDP; add them by hand. If the
  message says the search is unavailable, Gladys refused the SSDP access.
- **"No recent value" on a device**: the integration may be stopped; look at its logs in the
  **Supervision** tab.
- **Logs**: on the integration page in Gladys, or `docker logs` on the host. They stay quiet:
  the start, a host going offline or coming back, each Wake-on-LAN, and a problem once when it
  starts and once when it is over. `LOG_LEVEL=debug` shows every check.

## Limits

- IPv4 addresses and DNS names only; `.local` (mDNS) names are not resolved.
- Wake-on-LAN reaches the local network of the Gladys machine: waking a computer on another
  network (VPN, other VLAN) depends on your router forwarding broadcasts, which most do not.
- Gladys sends one magic packet every 2 seconds at most: waking ten computers at once takes
  20 seconds.
- A successful wake-up only means the packet left: only the next answers prove the device is on.
- 64 hosts at most. Each check sends 3 pings or, in TCP, up to 10 connection attempts per host;
  nothing leaves your network, no account and no cloud service are involved.
- What the integration stores: the list of hosts and their options, in `/data/hosts.json` in its
  container.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Ping & Wake-on-LAN asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your hosts | `section` | No | Add each computer, NAS, TV or phone to watch with the "Add or update a host" action below, then create its device in the Discover tab. "Search the network" proposes the devices that announce themselves (UPnP), with their MAC address when Gladys knows it. |
| Check interval | `select` | No | How often every host is checked. |
| Offline after | `select` | No | Time without any answer before a host is shown offline. Phones asleep on Wi-Fi skip answers: give them 5 to 10 minutes (per host, in the action below). |
| Wake-up timeout | `select` | No | How long a woken device has to answer before the "A device did not wake up" trigger fires. A packet is sent again every 30 seconds meanwhile. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Names given to the features of new devices (Online, Latency, Wake up) and language of the messages. |

## How to install Ping & Wake-on-LAN in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Ping & Wake-on-LAN appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-ping-wol:1.0.2`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-ping-wol](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-ping-wol).

Ping & Wake-on-LAN requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

Ping & Wake-on-LAN is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
